label: Glossary Terms
description: Terms are listed alphabetically under their first letter.

defaults.title: Ablation
defaults.scientificDefinition: Loss of ice or snow from a glacier due to melting, sublimation, or calving.
defaults.simpleDefinition: The glacier is shrinking as ice melts or breaks off.

defaults.title: Accumulation
defaults.scientificDefinition: The addition of snow and ice to a glacier, primarily through snowfall.
defaults.simpleDefinition: New snow builds up on the glacier, making it grow.

defaults.title: Alpine Glacier
defaults.scientificDefinition: A glacier formed in mountainous regions, typically flowing down valleys.
defaults.simpleDefinition: A mountain glacier moving like a slow river.

defaults.title: Arete
defaults.scientificDefinition: A sharp ridge formed between two glaciers eroding parallel valleys.
defaults.simpleDefinition: A narrow mountain ridge shaped by glaciers on both both sides.

defaults.title: Avalanche
defaults.scientificDefinition: A rapid flow of snow down a slope, often involving ice and debris.
defaults.simpleDefinition: A big rush of snow sliding down a mountain.

defaults.title: Ablation Zone
defaults.scientificDefinition: The lower part of a glacier where melting and ice loss exceed accumulation.
defaults.simpleDefinition: The part of the glacier that loses more ice than it gains.

defaults.title: Active Layer
defaults.scientificDefinition: The surface layer of soil above permafrost that thaws and refreezes annually.
defaults.simpleDefinition: The top soil that melts in summer and freezes again in winter.

defaults.title: Arctic Amplification
defaults.scientificDefinition: The phenomenon where the Arctic warms faster than the global average due to feedback mechanisms.
defaults.simpleDefinition: The Arctic is heating up faster than the rest of the world.

defaults.title: Bergschrund
defaults.scientificDefinition: A deep crevasse separating moving glacier ice from the stagnant ice or rock at the head of a glacier.
defaults.simpleDefinition: A big crack near the top of a glacier.

defaults.title: Basal Sliding
defaults.scientificDefinition: The movement of glacier ice over the bedrock, lubricated by meltwater.
defaults.simpleDefinition: The glacier slips over wet ground underneath.

defaults.title: Blue Ice
defaults.scientificDefinition: Densely packed glacier ice that appears blue due to the absorption of red light.
defaults.simpleDefinition: Very old, dense glacier ice that looks blue.

defaults.title: Brittle Zone
defaults.scientificDefinition: The upper glacier layer where ice breaks under stress, forming crevasses.
defaults.simpleDefinition: The top part of the glacier where cracks easily form.

defaults.title: Bedrock
defaults.scientificDefinition: The solid rock beneath glacier ice or soil.
defaults.simpleDefinition: The hard rock under the glacier.

defaults.title: Basal Melt
defaults.scientificDefinition: Melting of glacier ice at its base due to geothermal heat or friction.
defaults.simpleDefinition: Ice melting at the bottom of the glacier.

defaults.title: Basal Till
defaults.scientificDefinition: Sediment deposited directly under a glacier as it moves.
defaults.simpleDefinition: Mud and rocks left behind by a moving glacier.

defaults.title: Black Carbon
defaults.scientificDefinition: Soot particles that settle on glaciers, reducing albedo and accelerating melt.
defaults.simpleDefinition: Dark dust on ice that makes glaciers melt faster.

defaults.title: Crevasse
defaults.scientificDefinition: A deep crack or fracture in the glacier surface caused by stress.
defaults.simpleDefinition: A big crack on top of a glacier.

defaults.title: Cirque
defaults.scientificDefinition: A bowl-shaped depression carved by a glacier at the head of a valley.
defaults.simpleDefinition: A big scoop in the mountain where a glacier started.

defaults.title: Continental Glacier
defaults.scientificDefinition: Massive ice sheets covering large land areas like Antarctica or Greenland.
defaults.simpleDefinition: A huge glacier covering a whole continent.

defaults.title: Calving
defaults.scientificDefinition: The breaking off of ice chunks from the edge of a glacier, often forming icebergs.
defaults.simpleDefinition: When pieces of glacier fall into the ocean.

defaults.title: Cryosphere
defaults.scientificDefinition: All frozen water parts on Earth, including glaciers, ice caps, and permafrost.
defaults.simpleDefinition: All the icy places on Earth.

defaults.title: Cold-based Glacier
defaults.scientificDefinition: A glacier frozen to its bed, with little or no movement at the base.
defaults.simpleDefinition: A glacier stuck to the ground with no sliding.

defaults.title: Cryoconite
defaults.scientificDefinition: Dark dust on glacier surfaces that absorbs heat and speeds up melting.
defaults.simpleDefinition: Dirty spots on a glacier that make it melt faster.

defaults.title: Climate Change
defaults.scientificDefinition: Long-term change in global temperatures and weather patterns affecting glacier dynamics.
defaults.simpleDefinition: The Earth is getting warmer, which melts glaciers.

defaults.title: Core Sampling
defaults.scientificDefinition: A method of extracting ice cylinders to study past climate.
defaults.simpleDefinition: Taking deep ice samples to learn about Earth’s history.

defaults.title: Carbon Sink
defaults.scientificDefinition: A natural system that absorbs more carbon than it releases. Glaciers may indirectly act as carbon sinks through ecosystems.
defaults.simpleDefinition: Nature storing away harmful gases.

defaults.title: Debris-covered Glacier
defaults.scientificDefinition: A glacier whose surface is partially or fully covered with rock debris.
defaults.simpleDefinition: A glacier hidden under a layer of rocks.

defaults.title: Drumlin
defaults.scientificDefinition: A streamlined hill formed beneath a glacier, shaped by ice movement and till.
defaults.simpleDefinition: A smooth, long hill made by a glacier.

defaults.title: Delta
defaults.scientificDefinition: A landform at the mouth of a river where sediment is deposited as the water flow slows.
defaults.simpleDefinition: A fan-shaped area where a glacier-fed river ends.

defaults.title: Deflation
defaults.scientificDefinition: Wind-driven removal of fine sediment from a glacier's surface.
defaults.simpleDefinition: Wind blowing away dust from a glacier.

defaults.title: Erratic
defaults.scientificDefinition: A large rock transported by a glacier far from its origin.
defaults.simpleDefinition: A big boulder left behind by a glacier in a strange place.

defaults.title: Esker
defaults.scientificDefinition: A winding ridge formed from sediments deposited by meltwater streams beneath a glacier.
defaults.simpleDefinition: A long, twisty hill made by water under a glacier.

defaults.title: Englacial
defaults.scientificDefinition: Located within the glacier ice.
defaults.simpleDefinition: Something stuck inside a glacier.

defaults.title: Equilibrium Line
defaults.scientificDefinition: The dividing line on a glacier between the accumulation and ablation zones.
defaults.simpleDefinition: Where the glacier neither grows nor shrinks.

defaults.title: Firn
defaults.scientificDefinition: Granular snow that has survived one melt season but has not yet turned into ice.
defaults.simpleDefinition: Snow that’s a bit like ice but not quite.

defaults.title: Fjord
defaults.scientificDefinition: A deep, glacially carved valley flooded by seawater.
defaults.simpleDefinition: A deep sea inlet made by glaciers.

defaults.title: Flow Line
defaults.scientificDefinition: Path followed by particles within a glacier as it moves.
defaults.simpleDefinition: The glacier’s trail as it slowly flows downhill.

defaults.title: Freeze-Thaw Weathering
defaults.scientificDefinition: The breaking of rock due to water freezing and expanding in cracks.
defaults.simpleDefinition: When water freezes in cracks and breaks rocks.

defaults.title: Glacier
defaults.scientificDefinition: A large, persistent body of ice that forms on land and moves under its own weight.
defaults.simpleDefinition: A big, slow-moving river of ice.

defaults.title: Glacial Retreat
defaults.scientificDefinition: The process of a glacier shrinking back due to melting and reduced snowfall.
defaults.simpleDefinition: When a glacier melts and gets smaller.

defaults.title: Glacial Advance
defaults.scientificDefinition: When a glacier grows and moves forward.
defaults.simpleDefinition: The glacier is growing and sliding ahead.

defaults.title: Glacial Erratic
defaults.scientificDefinition: A large rock carried and deposited by a glacier far from its source.
defaults.simpleDefinition: A big rock out of place thanks to a glacier.

defaults.title: Horn
defaults.scientificDefinition: A sharp mountain peak formed by glacial erosion from multiple sides.
defaults.simpleDefinition: A pointed mountain carved by glaciers.

defaults.title: Hanging Valley
defaults.scientificDefinition: A smaller valley left above the main valley, often with waterfalls, after glacial erosion.
defaults.simpleDefinition: A side valley that hangs above a bigger one.

defaults.title: Hydrofracture
defaults.scientificDefinition: Cracking of ice due to water pressure.
defaults.simpleDefinition: Water breaking through glacier ice.

defaults.title: Hydrology
defaults.scientificDefinition: The study of water flow and storage in glacier systems.
defaults.simpleDefinition: How water moves in and around glaciers.

defaults.title: Ice Cap
defaults.scientificDefinition: A dome-shaped glacier covering less than 50,000 square kilometers.
defaults.simpleDefinition: A smaller ice sheet over land.

defaults.title: Ice Sheet
defaults.scientificDefinition: A massive glacier covering more than 50,000 square kilometers.
defaults.simpleDefinition: A giant slab of ice over a large area.

defaults.title: Iceberg
defaults.scientificDefinition: A large chunk of ice that broke off from a glacier and floats in the ocean.
defaults.simpleDefinition: A piece of glacier floating in water.

defaults.title: Icefall
defaults.scientificDefinition: A steep section of a glacier with rapid ice flow and crevasses.
defaults.simpleDefinition: A frozen waterfall made of glacier ice.

defaults.title: Jokulhlaup
defaults.scientificDefinition: A sudden, glacial outburst flood.
defaults.simpleDefinition: A surprise flood from a glacier.

defaults.title: Kettle Lake
defaults.scientificDefinition: A lake formed when a buried chunk of glacier ice melts.
defaults.simpleDefinition: A small lake left behind by melting glacier ice.

defaults.title: Kame
defaults.scientificDefinition: A hill made of sand and gravel deposited by meltwater.
defaults.simpleDefinition: A mound formed by water from a melting glacier.

defaults.title: Lateral Moraine
defaults.scientificDefinition: A ridge of debris deposited along the sides of a glacier.
defaults.simpleDefinition: A rocky edge next to a glacier.

defaults.title: Loess
defaults.scientificDefinition: Fine, wind-blown sediment from glacial outwash plains.
defaults.simpleDefinition: Dusty soil blown from glacier areas.

defaults.title: Lag Deposit
defaults.scientificDefinition: Coarse material left behind after finer sediments are blown or washed away.
defaults.simpleDefinition: The heavier stuff left behind when the light stuff is blown off.

defaults.title: Moraine
defaults.scientificDefinition: An accumulation of debris deposited by a glacier.
defaults.simpleDefinition: A pile of rocks and dirt from a glacier.

defaults.title: Medial Moraine
defaults.scientificDefinition: A stripe of debris formed where two glaciers meet.
defaults.simpleDefinition: A line of rocks in the middle of a glacier.

defaults.title: Mass Balance
defaults.scientificDefinition: The difference between accumulation and ablation on a glacier.
defaults.simpleDefinition: Whether a glacier is growing or shrinking overall.

defaults.title: Meltwater
defaults.scientificDefinition: Water from melting glacier ice.
defaults.simpleDefinition: Melted ice from the glacier.

defaults.title: Neve
defaults.scientificDefinition: Compacted snow that is in the process of becoming glacier ice.
defaults.simpleDefinition: Snow that’s turning into glacier ice.

defaults.title: Nunatak
defaults.scientificDefinition: A mountain peak or rocky ridge that sticks out above a glacier.
defaults.simpleDefinition: A rocky island sticking up out of the ice.

defaults.title: Outwash Plain
defaults.scientificDefinition: Flat area formed by sediment deposited by meltwater from a glacier.
defaults.simpleDefinition: A flat land made from melted glacier water and dirt.

defaults.title: Overdeepening
defaults.scientificDefinition: When glaciers erode bedrock to form deep basins below sea level.
defaults.simpleDefinition: A deep hole carved under the glacier.

defaults.title: Permafrost
defaults.scientificDefinition: Ground that stays frozen for at least two years.
defaults.simpleDefinition: Soil that’s always frozen.

defaults.title: Plucking
defaults.scientificDefinition: A glacier pulling rocks away from the ground as it moves.
defaults.simpleDefinition: The glacier yanks rocks from the ground.

defaults.title: Piedmont Glacier
defaults.scientificDefinition: A glacier that spreads out at the base of a mountain range.
defaults.simpleDefinition: A glacier that flattens out when it hits a plain.

defaults.title: Quaternary Glaciation
defaults.scientificDefinition: The most recent period of ice ages spanning the last 2.6 million years.
defaults.simpleDefinition: The time of Earth’s recent ice ages.

defaults.title: Roche Moutonnée
defaults.scientificDefinition: A rock formation smoothed by glacier ice on one side and steep on the other.
defaults.simpleDefinition: A rock shaped by glaciers, smooth on one side, rough on the other.

defaults.title: Rift
defaults.scientificDefinition: A crack or gap formed by ice pulling apart.
defaults.simpleDefinition: A split in the glacier.

defaults.title: Snowline
defaults.scientificDefinition: The lowest elevation where snow remains year-round.
defaults.simpleDefinition: The height on a mountain where snow doesn’t melt.

defaults.title: Surge
defaults.scientificDefinition: A short, rapid advance of a glacier.
defaults.simpleDefinition: When the glacier suddenly moves fast.

defaults.title: Sublimation
defaults.scientificDefinition: Ice turning straight into vapor without melting first.
defaults.simpleDefinition: Ice disappearing into air without becoming water.

defaults.title: Terminus
defaults.scientificDefinition: The end or snout of a glacier.
defaults.simpleDefinition: The bottom or end of a glacier.

defaults.title: Tarn
defaults.scientificDefinition: A lake formed in a cirque after a glacier melts.
defaults.simpleDefinition: A small lake left in a mountain bowl.

defaults.title: Till
defaults.scientificDefinition: Unsorted sediment deposited directly by a glacier.
defaults.simpleDefinition: A mix of rocks and dirt dropped by a glacier.

defaults.title: U-shaped Valley
defaults.scientificDefinition: A valley with a rounded bottom carved by glacier movement.
defaults.simpleDefinition: A valley shaped like a big “U.”

defaults.title: Valley Glacier
defaults.scientificDefinition: A glacier that flows down a mountain valley.
defaults.simpleDefinition: A glacier squeezed into a mountain path.

defaults.title: Vegetation Feedback
defaults.scientificDefinition: How plants growing on glacial land can affect melting and climate.
defaults.simpleDefinition: Plants growing on glaciers can speed up melting.

defaults.title: White Ice
defaults.scientificDefinition: Newly fallen or less compressed glacier ice that appears white.
defaults.simpleDefinition: Fresh or fluffy-looking glacier ice.

defaults.title: Watershed
defaults.scientificDefinition: A land area where all the water drains to one place, influenced by glaciers.
defaults.simpleDefinition: Where melted glacier water flows into rivers.

defaults.title: Xerothermic Period
defaults.scientificDefinition: A hot and dry climatic phase often used in paleoclimatic studies.
defaults.simpleDefinition: A very warm, dry time in Earth’s history.

defaults.title: Yenisei Glacier Influence
defaults.scientificDefinition: Refers to glacial impact on the Yenisei River system in Siberia.
defaults.simpleDefinition: How glaciers shaped the rivers in Siberia.

defaults.title: Younger Dryas
defaults.scientificDefinition: A sudden return to glacial conditions about 12,800 years ago.
defaults.simpleDefinition: A short, cold period during the end of the last ice age.

defaults.title: Zone of Ablation
defaults.scientificDefinition: The area of a glacier where ice loss exceeds gain.
defaults.simpleDefinition: Where the glacier melts more than it grows.

defaults.title: Zone of Accumulation
defaults.scientificDefinition: The region where snowfall adds to the glacier.
defaults.simpleDefinition: Where snow keeps adding ice to the glacier.
